question: The minimum period of time taken upto which the weather variations are considered to predict the climate of a place is ___________years.
solution:
The correct answer is __**30**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The minimum period of time taken up to which the weather variations are considered to predict the climate of a place is **30 years.**
 
• **The climate **is the long-term form of weather, truly says that it is an average form of weather over a period of 30 years.
 
• Some of the meteorological aspects of climate that are commonly identified are **humidity, temperature, atmospheric pressure, precipitation, and wind.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **Weather **is the basic state of the atmosphere.

 
 
• It is described as the **degree to which it is cold & hot, dry or wet, clear or cloudy.**
 
• In the lowest level of the atmosphere which is called the troposphere, just below the stratosphere, most weather phenomena occur. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Major factors of Climate & Weather: 

 
 
• There are some major elements that are usually responsible for climate & weather change, which are as follows:
 
 
 
• Temperature: 
 
 
• It is basically an intensity or degree of heat present in an object or substance, especially according to a comparative scale and shown & measured by a thermometer. 
 
• Temperature is a physical property of matter that expresses that the weather is hot and cold.
 
• It is the form of thermal energy, present in all matter, which is the source of the occurrence of heat, a flow of energy when an object is in contact with another that is hotter or colder. 
 
 
 
• Humidity: 
 
 
• Humidity is the intentness of water vapor that's present in the air.
 
• Water vapor is the last or gaseous state of water, and is generally invisible to humans.
 
• Humidity indicates the likelihood for dew, precipitation, or fog to be present.
 
 
 
• Atmosphere Pressure: 
 
 
• Atmospheric pressure is basically a force in any area pushed by any surface by the weight of the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• This is because high-altitude places do not have sufficient air above them, pushing them down.
 
• Barometers are used to measure the pressure of the atmosphere.
 
 
 
• Precipitation & Meteorological phenomena: 
 
 
• Precipitation & Meteorological phenomena are also essential elements for climate change.
 
• On Earth, the general weather phenomena include rain, cloud, wind, snow, fog & dust storms.
